claims.note: Opening composite scenario ('a team re-runs its eval') is illustrative framing, not a measured incident; it carries no number and attributes nothing to a named party.

Sample disclosure and the four-questions framing: 13 calls, four shapes, one model, one host, seed 42, zero errors, N=20 matrix not run. Counts (13/13, 11/13) and the 'not run' statement are from run.jsonl and METHOD.md.

Counts were re-read from run.jsonl and cross-checked against flip_table.csv and normalise_selftest.txt; no rate is derived.

evidence_boundary: Local fixture measurement only: one CPU-only host, one model, one prompt fixture, 13 calls, shared with a concurrent stage workload. No vendor system was measured. Third-party documentation caches (src-ollama-api.md, src-ollama-modelfile.mdx, src-rfc8259.txt, src-vllm-reproducibility.html) sit in the working-tree evidence directory but are neither linked from the article nor listed in public_artifacts; the publisher copies only receipt-referenced first-party run records and artifacts. No third-party source download is offered to readers.
proposed_process_improvements: Supply-stage proposals for probe-based articles should carry a sample size that fits one research attempt on this host (N=3-4 per condition, ~13 calls, ~8 minutes), or be marked as needing a dedicated measurement window; the N=20 plan could not be executed in budget.

Reader-facing helpers promised in the original evidence plan (the normalise_tool_call function with its four edge cases) were not produced by the research stage; the write stage had to author and test them to keep the promise. The research stage's artifact list should include every promised helper.

presentation.selected_title: Ollama Tool Calls: Same Seed, Different Bytes
presentation.title_rationale: Frontloads the product and object the reader searched for (Ollama, tool calls) and states the one supported finding - identical sampling settings still produced differing serialised arguments - in 45 characters instead of 99. The mechanism, the sample size and the caveats that made the old headline unreadable (measuring method, 'before you trust an agent eval', '(2026)') move into the introduction, where the body already states N and says the counts are not rates. No universal determinism claim is made: 'Same Seed, Different Bytes' is exactly what 11/13 byte-identical with two order flips at temperature 0.0 supports.
presentation.visual_purpose: Explains the comparison method the article asks the reader to adopt: fix the request and seed, repeat the calls, then compare meaning separately from serialised bytes. It is a conceptual checklist and says so in its footer, so it illustrates procedure rather than reporting the 13-call result; scope is the method only and it displays no counts, rates or timings that could be mistaken for measurements.
presentation.alt: Three-step conceptual checklist for tool-call repeatability: fixed request and seed, repeated tool calls, then a semantic versus byte comparison, captioned 'Compare meaning separately from serialized bytes.'
